title: Hummus
subtitle: Classic Lebanese smooth chickpea and tahini dip
excerpt: Smooth hummus depends on three things: well-cooked chickpeas, good tahini, and enough lemon. This recipe makes a silky, pale version that keeps for a week in the fridge.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Lebanese hummus preparations and Ottolenghi/Sami Tamimi technique documentation.

recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the batch easily. Keeps in the fridge for 5 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Hummus keeps refrigerated for up to 5 days. Bring to room temperature and stir before serving; add a splash of cold water and re-blend if it has thickened.

content.text: The secret to very smooth hummus is blending the tahini and lemon juice together first, before adding anything else. This emulsifies the tahini and produces a lighter, creamier texture. A food processor works well; a high-speed blender gives an even smoother result. The chickpea skins also affect smoothness: removing them after cooking is tedious but makes a noticeable difference if you want truly silky hummus.

items.prepNote: one tin, drained and rinsed (reserve the liquid)
crushed to a paste with a little salt
good extra-virgin, plus more to serve

content.text: Warm the chickpeas. Tip the drained chickpeas into a small saucepan with a pinch of bicarbonate of soda (if you have it; this softens the skins) and cover with cold water. Bring to the boil, then drain and rinse. This step also makes them blend more smoothly. Optional: rub the chickpeas between your palms to remove the skins; they will float off in the rinse water.

Emulsify the tahini and lemon. Put the tahini and lemon juice in the food processor. Process for 2 full minutes until the mixture turns pale and thick, almost like peanut butter. This is the most important step: do not skip it.
Add the garlic and spice. Add the garlic paste and cumin to the processor and blitz for 30 seconds.

Add the chickpeas. Add the warm chickpeas to the processor. Blend for 3 to 4 minutes, scraping down the sides regularly. While the processor is running, add the olive oil through the spout. Then add the reserved chickpea liquid, one tablespoon at a time, until the hummus is silky and loose enough to spread easily. You may need 3 to 5 tablespoons.

Season and serve. Taste and adjust: more lemon for brightness, more salt, more garlic. Spoon into a wide bowl, use the back of a spoon to create a swirl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with smoked paprika. Scatter over the parsley leaves if using. Serve with warm flatbread or crudites.

items.symptom: Hummus is grainy rather than smooth
items.cause: The processor did not run for long enough, or the chickpeas were not warm when blended.
items.fix: Keep blending: 4 minutes total is often needed. Warm chickpeas blend far more smoothly than cold ones. Add another tablespoon of chickpea liquid and blend for another minute.

items.cause: Too much tahini, or the tahini used was very strong.
items.fix: Add more lemon juice. Tahini quality varies: look for Lebanese or Palestinian brands, which tend to be milder and creamier than some others.

items.symptom: Hummus is too thick and pasty
items.cause: Not enough liquid was added during blending.
items.fix: Add chickpea liquid or cold water one tablespoon at a time, processor running, until smooth and spreadable.
